title: Facilitates Bayesian Analysis using STAN with CmdStanR
text: smbr2 (pronounced simber two) R package facilitate analyses using STAN cmdstanr. smbr2 developed alternative smbr. uses cmdstanr instead rstan model-fitting engine. begin using smbr2, must install CmdStan running check_cmdstan_toolchain() cmdstanr::install_cmdstan(). installation instructions see . motivation using cmdstanr stays --date recent developments Stan dev team (.e., via CmdStan). smbr2 able incorporate improved functionality new Stan syntax, faster parallelization, progress communication parallelization, pedantic Stan model checking, Stan model diagnostics summary, model fitting alternative engines pathfinder, Laplace approximation, variational inference, optimization. Note S3 methods class smb_model smb_code imported smbr. smbr smbr2 part embr family packages. enable smbr2 functionality embr, modify stan_engine argument embr::analyse(), e.g. embr::analyse(stan_engine = 'cmdstan-mcmc'). new Stan syntax must used. smbr2 fail old Stan syntax. don’t wish update old model, simply leave stan_engine argument default, use smbr instead.

title: Facilitates Bayesian Analysis using STAN with CmdStanR
code: library(bauw) library(ggplot2) library(magrittr) library(embr) library(smbr2)  # define model in Stan language model <- model(code = "   data {       int nAnnual;       int nObs;       array[nObs] int Annual;       array[nObs] int Pairs;       array[nObs] real Year;   }   parameters {       vector[nAnnual] bAnnual;       real log_sAnnual;       real alpha;       real beta1;       real beta2;       real beta3;   }   transformed parameters {     real sAnnual;     sAnnual = exp(log_sAnnual);   }   model {       vector[nObs] ePairs;       log_sAnnual ~ normal(0, 10);       bAnnual ~ normal(0, sAnnual);       alpha ~ normal(0, 10);       beta1 ~ normal(0, 10);       beta2 ~ normal(0, 10);       beta3 ~ normal(0, 10);       for (i in 1:nObs) {         ePairs[i] = exp(alpha + beta1 * Year[i] + beta2 * Year[i]^2 +                       beta3 * Year[i]^3 + bAnnual[Annual[i]]);       }       target += poisson_lpmf(Pairs | ePairs);   } ")  # add R code to calculate derived parameters model %<>% update_model(new_expr = "   for (i in 1:length(Pairs)) {     prediction[i] <- exp(alpha + beta1 * Year[i] + beta2 * Year[i]^2 +                        beta3 * Year[i]^3 + bAnnual[Annual[i]])   } ")  # define data types and center year model %<>% update_model(   select_data = list(     "Pairs" = integer(), "Year*" = integer(),     Annual = factor()   ),   derived = "sAnnual",   random_effects = list(bAnnual = "Annual") )  data <- bauw::peregrine data$Annual <- factor(data$Year)  set.seed(42)  # analyse analysis <- analyse(model, data = data, seed = 3L, glance = FALSE, stan_engine = "cmdstan-mcmc")  # analyse pathfinder analysis_path <- analyse(model, data = data, seed = 3L, glance = FALSE, stan_engine = "cmdstan-pathfinder")  # coefficient table coef(analysis, simplify = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 5 × 5 #>   term        estimate   lower   upper svalue #>   <term>         <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1 alpha         4.26    4.18    4.34    9.97  #> 2 beta1         1.19    1.06    1.33    9.97  #> 3 beta2        -0.0191 -0.0735  0.0401  0.937 #> 4 beta3        -0.272  -0.345  -0.207   9.97  #> 5 log_sAnnual  -2.24   -2.81   -1.80    9.97  coef(analysis_path, simplify = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 5 × 5 #>   term        estimate   lower   upper svalue #>   <term>         <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1 alpha        4.25     4.21    4.30     8.97 #> 2 beta1        1.24     1.17    1.28     8.97 #> 3 beta2       -0.00877 -0.0531  0.0139   1.60 #> 4 beta3       -0.298   -0.321  -0.259    8.97 #> 5 log_sAnnual -2.23    -2.56   -2.10     8.97  # trace plots plot(analysis) # make predictions by varying year with other predictors including the random effect of Annual held constant year <- predict(analysis, new_data = "Year") year_path <- predict(analysis_path, new_data = "Year")  years <- dplyr::bind_rows(list("mcmc" = year, "pathfinder" = year_path), .id = "engine")  # plot those predictions ggplot(data = years, aes(x = Year, y = estimate)) +   geom_point(data = bauw::peregrine, aes(y = Pairs)) +   geom_line(aes(color = engine)) +   geom_line(aes(y = lower, color = engine), linetype = "dotted") +   geom_line(aes(y = upper, color = engine), linetype = "dotted") +   expand_limits(y = 0)

text: tibble one row containing: n Number observations dataset K Number parameters nchains Number MCMC chains niters Number iterations per chain (post-warmup) nthin Thinning interval converged Logical indicating convergence. TRUE : max(rhat) less equal threshold, min(ESS) greater equal threshold, perc_divergent less euqal threshold. Problem indicators: value > 0% indicates sampling issues perc_max_treedepth Percentage transitions hit maximum tree depth. Problem indicators: Values > 0% may indicate inefficient sampling ebfmi Minimum Energy Bayesian Fraction Missing Information across chains. Problem indicators: Values < 0.2 indicate poor adaptation/warmup

title: Glance at CmdStanR MCMC Analysis — glance.cmdstan_mcmc_analysis
text: Diagnostic interpretation: Divergent transitions: ideally 0. divergent transitions indicate sampler numerical issues results may unreliable. Max treedepth: ideally 0 low. High values suggest sampler working hard may benefit reparameterization. Increasing max treedepth also option generally discouraged since increases model fitting times without addressing underlying issue. High max treedepth necessarily indicate convergence issues. E-BFMI: > 0.2. Values < 0.2 suggest poor adaptation, often requiring longer warmup model reparameterization. However, sensitivity problematic diagnostics depends analysis mode set via embr::set_analysis_mode(). 'paper' mode mode requires divergent transitions 0% – modes accept level tolerance.
